scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Record Group 6 contains information on the Commission of Intercollegiate Athletics and the Knight Commission on Information Needs of Communities in a Democracy.

did.unittitle: Knight Commission on Intercollegiate Athletics

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Commission of Intercollegiate Athletics was formed in 1989 to survey and discuss corruption and abuses in college athletic programs and to make recommendations for reform.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains correspondence regarding the creation (and later reconvening) of the Commission in Intercollegiate Athletics task force, its subsequent works, and all its reports.

did.unittitle: "A Call To Action: Reconnecting College Sports and Higher Education"

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: "A Call to Action: Reconnecting College Sports and Higher Education", report of the Knight Foundation Commission on Intercollegiate Athletics. As the 10th anniversary of the Commission's first report in March 1991 approached, the members of the Commission decided to reconvene for a fresh look at what has happened in this intervening decade and to assess the state of college athletics at the beginning of this new century. This report presents the Commission's finding from a series of meetings with NCAA representatives, university officials, athletic directors coaches, athlettes and others. 3 copies

did.unittitle: Knight Commission on Information Needs of Communities in a Democracy

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Knight Commission on Information Needs of Communities in a Democracy, established in 2008 by Knight Foundation President, Alberto Ibarguen. As a joint project of the Knight Foundation and the Aspen Institute Communications and Society Program, the Commission's goal is to recommend both public and private measures that would help American communities better meet their information needs. With a research-based approach, the commission examines the following questions: What are the information needs of communities in our American Democracy? What are the current trends affecting how community information needs are met? And what changes will ensure that community information l be better met in the future?

did.unittitle: Technology for Engagement Summit program

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Includes a KF News Release on the initiative; and information on the 2012 Summit Meeting. The summit, which took place at the MIT Media Lab, was designed to explore "where we are and imagine where we might go together in the field of technology and engagement." Several KF staffers participated in the summit. KF's Technology for Engagement initiative funds innovative, digital technologies that inspire civic dialogue and collective community action. The program lists a schedule and biographies of participants. Also included is information on two other meetings: TED2013 Knight Foundation: Ideas into Action (Introductory comments & Context setting with Damian Thorman, June Cohen and Matt Saiia); and the GovLab Experiment: Making Engagement Work; and an Evaluation of Tech for Engagement Initiative at Knight Foundation: What is the Most Effective Business Model? by Crystal Ward, National Urban Fellows Program.
